ingredients: 1.5 cups Arborio rice (do not rinse, as starch is needed)
5 to 6 cups vegetable broth (kept warm in a separate pot)
1 lb mixed mushrooms (cremini, shiitake, oyster), sliced
2 tbsp vegan butter (or extra olive oil)
0.25 cup nutritional yeast (optional, for cheesy flavor)
Salt and black pepper to taste

instructions.title: Warm the Broth
instructions.text: Pour the vegetable broth into a saucepan and keep it on a low simmer next to your main cooking pot. Cold broth shocks the rice and stops the cooking process, preventing the creamy texture from developing.

instructions.title: Sauté the Mushrooms
instructions.text: In your heavy-bottomed pot, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil over medium-high heat. Add the sliced mushrooms and cook until browned and their liquid has evaporated (about 5-8 minutes). Season with a pinch of salt. Remove mushrooms from the pot and set aside. This prevents them from getting rubbery during the rice cooking.

instructions.title: Aromatics and Toasting
instructions.text: Reduce heat to medium. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil to the pot. Add shallots and cook until softened (2-3 minutes). Add garlic and thyme, cooking for another minute until fragrant. Add the Arborio rice. Toast the rice, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes until the edges are translucent and the center remains opaque. This toasting step creates a shell around the grain so it doesn't turn to mush while slowly releasing starch.

instructions.title: Deglaze
instructions.text: Pour in the white wine. Stir constantly until the wine is fully absorbed by the rice.

instructions.title: The Risotto Method
instructions.text: Begin adding the warm broth, one ladle (about 0.5 cup) at a time. Stir frequently. Wait until the liquid is almost completely absorbed before adding the next ladle. The friction from stirring rubs the grains together, releasing the starch that creates the creamy sauce. Repeat this process for about 20-25 minutes. The rice is done when it is tender but still has a slight bite (al dente).

instructions.title: The Finish (Mantecatura)
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. This is crucial. Stir in the cooked mushrooms, vegan butter, and nutritional yeast. Vigorously stir the mixture for 30 seconds to emulsify the fats with the starch. This step guarantees the creamy mouthfeel without dairy. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Garnish with fresh parsley and serve immediately.

phases.action: Chop vegetables, slice mushrooms, warm broth

props.text: This recipe creates a rich, velvety risotto for 4 people without using dairy. The key to the creamy texture lies in the high starch content of Arborio rice and the agitation process (stirring), which releases that starch into the broth. We will use a mix of mushrooms for depth of flavor and finish with a "mantecatura" technique using vegan fat to emulsify the sauce.

This recipe assumes you have a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven to distribute heat evenly. We assume the use of dry white wine (like Pinot Grigio or Sauvignon Blanc) to deglaze the pan, but you can substitute extra vegetable broth mixed with a teaspoon of lemon juice or white wine vinegar if you prefer an alcohol-free version. We also assume the use of store-bought low-sodium vegetable broth, but homemade stock works excellently.

props.text: These recommendations assume the group has little to no prior experience with modern hobby board games. The selections focus on high interaction, minimal downtime between turns, and rules that can be taught in under 5 minutes. The games selected bridge the gap between casual conversation and structured play, ensuring the 60-minute time limit is respected even with teaching time included.

The group splits into two teams, Red and Blue. Each team has a Spymaster who provides one-word clues linked to multiple cards on the table. The goal is for teammates to guess the correct words based on the clue without picking the opposing team's words or the instant-loss Assassin card. It encourages clever thinking and group discussion.

This is a fully cooperative game where everyone wins or loses together. One player is the guesser, and the other five write one-word clues to help them guess a specific word. The catch is that if any two players write the exact same clue, those clues are erased and the guesser never sees them. It forces players to be creative rather than obvious.

One player is secretly the Murderer, and another is the Forensic Scientist who knows the solution but can only communicate by placing markers on scene tiles (like Cause of Death: Suffocation). The remaining players are investigators trying to interpret these vague clues to identify the murderer and the weapon used. It is less aggressive than other lying games because the focus is on the evidence.

Players are members of a resistance group trying to overthrow a government, but spies have infiltrated the ranks. In each round, a leader proposes a team to go on a mission. Everyone votes to approve the team. If the mission goes ahead, players on the team secretly choose to Support or Sabotage the mission. The goal is to deduce who the saboteurs are based on voting patterns and mission results.

props.text: Visiting Kyoto in early April places you in the peak of spring season. While cherry blossoms (sakura) may be starting to flutter down by April 5-7, the city will be vibrant and busy. This itinerary balances the crowds by mixing popular historical sites with ample outdoor space for children.

To accommodate children ages 8 and 10 and the walking constraints, this plan utilizes a "hub" approach where you visit one major area in the morning and one in the afternoon. A taxi is recommended for the steep hill to Kiyomizu-dera. Early April averages 10-20°C (50-68°F) and rain is possible.
Iwatayama Monkey Park & Bamboo Grove | West Kyoto
Start at JR Saga-Arashiyama Station. Walk 15 minutes to the Monkey Park entrance for an easy 20-minute trail. Afterward, cross the Togetsukyo Bridge to the Bamboo Grove.
Fushimi Inari Shrine & Kiyomizu-dera | Southern & Eastern Kyoto
Morning at Fushimi Inari (JR Inari Station is adjacent). The lower loop hike is gentle. Afternoon: Take a taxi to Kiyomizu-dera to avoid the steep approach walk.
Kinkaku-ji Temple & Kyoto Railway Museum | North & Central
Morning: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion). Access via taxi or direct bus. Afternoon: Kyoto Railway Museum (adjacent to Umekoji-Kyotonishi Station), which is interactive and ideal for ages 8-10.

props.text: January is widely considered the peak travel season for both cities, but for very different reasons. Bangkok experiences its "cool" season, which is dry and sunny but still hot by global standards. Hanoi experiences a true winter, which is significantly cooler and often overcast with mist. For a walking tour, Hanoi offers much more comfortable temperatures, while Bangkok guarantees brighter photography conditions at the cost of heat exhaustion risks.

January weather patterns in Southeast Asia are generally stable, but short-term fluctuations can occur.
